facts.text: MazeEnvSample5x5 loads the pre-generated maze file maze2d_5x5.npy, a 5x5 world
The action space is Discrete(2*len(maze_size)), so the 5x5 sample maze has four integer actions
ACTION lists the four directions N, S, E, W
An integer action is an index into ACTION; step calls move_robot with that direction
If the destination is blocked, move_robot does not move the robot
is_open requires the destination to be inside the grid and allows the move when either side of the shared wall is open
The observation space is a two-element Box of integers from 0 to maze_size-1
The entrance is cell (0, 0) and the goal is the last cell, maze_size - (1, 1)
reset puts the robot back at the entrance, sets state to zeros(2), clears steps_beyond_done, sets done False and returns the state
A step gives reward 1 and done True at the goal, otherwise reward -0.1/(maze_size[0]*maze_size[1]) and done False
step returns the legacy four-tuple (state, reward, done, info) and has no truncated flag
MazeEnv.seed seeds a numpy random generator and returns [seed]
reset takes no arguments and returns the fixed zero state; it does not draw from the generator set by seed
step moves the robot on the fixed maze data and does not draw from a random generator
maze-v0 is registered to MazeEnvSample5x5 with max_episode_steps=2000
The upstream package declares gym, pygame and numpy as install requirements

determinism.notes: the sample maze and the start cell are fixed and every step is a deterministic grid transition; MazeEnv.seed exists but reset and step never draw from its generator, so a seed is echoed and does not change a trajectory. The bridge's state_hash also counts the episode, so two runs compare from a fresh world or from the same episode ordinal.

gaps: no physics and no continuous time: one tick is one grid-cell transition on a fixed 5x5 wall layout, so timestep_ms is 0 (an event-driven analytic model)
no wall-clock pacing and no rendering: the pygame viewer and the rgb_array image are not modelled; cap.world.render.v1 stays unbound

the fake re-implements the MazeEnv and MazeView2D grid rules in pure Python and embeds the shipped 5x5 wall layout as test data; it was not compared with a run of the upstream environment (gym, pygame and numpy are not imported where the gate runs)

the raw MazeEnv.step returns a four-tuple and never truncates; the fake emulates the 2000-step TimeLimit that gym.make adds to maze-v0 (gym_maze/__init__.py:7), so the bridge reports truncated at 2000 ticks
only the fixed 5x5 sample environment is modelled, not the random, portal or loop variants, and the observation is a plain two-element array rather than a numpy int64 array
snapshot and restore are not offered: MazeEnv exposes no get_state or set_state

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the maze state is kept and stays readable
